newsitem.title: UK: Lira skids as worries of EMU delay for Italy mount.
newsitem.headline: Lira skids as worries of EMU delay for Italy mount.

text.p: The lira skidded to within a whisker of its European exchange rate mechanism central rate at 990 per mark on Tuesday amid concern about its omission from the first wave of European monetary union.
Dealers said the Bank of Italy monitored lira prices closely and was prepared to intervene to sell marks above 990 lire.

Traders and analysts cited a combination of comments from Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi late Monday and reported newspaper comments from Belgian central bank chief Alfonse Verplaetse as hurting the Italian currency and bond market.
Verplaetse later denied his comments referred to Italy.

Belgian newspaper De Financieel Economische Tijd quoted Verplaetse as saying: "I would not mind seeing countries with a government deficit of seven percent (of gross domestic product) lowering their deficit to three percent in a year's time and in a durable way. In my view, that is not possible."
At 1000 GMT in London, the lira was at 989.75 per mark compared with 985.55 earlier and 987.25 late Monday.

"Prodi's exasperation at (German Chancellor Helmut) Kohl yesterday seem to show he suspects plot against Italy joining in the first wave and the comments from Belgium today suggest the EU core is ganging up against Italy," said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at Dutch bank ABN Amro in London
Prodi said on Monday Germany was less committed to EMU that Italy. "We see our future in Europe. I don't know if that is the case in Germany," he said.

"The market is sensing a delay for Italy is in the offing. Italian bond yield spreads are widening again and dragging the lira lower," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Germany's Commerzbank in London.
The higher dollar/mark, above 1.70 for the first time in 34 months, may limit lira losses, however, as traders are reluctant to buy an independently weak mark, he said.
Norfield at ABN Amro said the Bank of Italy would be expected to sell some of its substantial foreign exchange reserves to buoy the currency but a move higher to 995 per mark is likely.

Both Norfield and Ferridge said the best way to exploit lira weakness is to buy dollars for lira, to take advantage of the dollar's broad-based ascent against European currencies and further potential lira weakness against the mark.
The dollar/lira has surged 11.5 percent since the start of the year and could have another few percent at least to rise, they said.
